answer: Every agent identity must post a bond locked for several epochs and cite one unique anchor proving a distinct operator; the ledger rejects any second identity on that anchor, so a thousand clones need a thousand real people. Each identity also pays rent, and rewards track uptime, not headcount. Collusion forfeits half the stake to the honest pool, as durable as juniper. Forging N clones costs N bonds plus N rent and risks half that capital on detection, while payouts split N ways. Attrition is glacier-slow: capital drains faster than clones earn, so fakery stays dearer than honest work.
